close_reason: Positive observation, no action required. The 40-line module-level rustdoc 'Single-user limitation' section at memory.rs:43-83 is the right shape for a reference impl. Closing as 'noted, what good looks like'.
description:
Why this is good: The 40-line module-level rustdoc 'Single-user limitation (per-caller scoping is NOT implemented)' section explicitly:
- Names the limitation (per-user uniqueness, isPrivate visibility scoping).
- Names the spec sections that require correction (§3.1 per-user uniqueness, §1.2.1 isPrivate scoping).
- Lists THREE concrete things a real backend MUST do, with code-level specificity (scope find_uniqueness_conflict, filter Metadata/get by principal, reject /set updates against non-authored private records).
- Acknowledges that the reference impl's JmapBackend::principal_id returns None, and explains WHY wiring it would not change behavior in the single-user case.

A future contributor might suggest 'simplifying' this by trimming to one sentence ('Single-user only; production backends must do their own scoping'). That would lose the call-site-level specificity that makes the disclosure actionable. Defend against simplification: the SECTIONS_LIKE_THIS_ARE_THE_WHOLE_POINT of a 'reference implementation' — the explicit list of which call sites need adapting is more valuable than the code itself.

Cross-reference: workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)' section. Metadata-server's memory.rs is the only crate so far that operationalizes the rule into specific call-site guidance. Mail-server lacks the same disclosure (filed as JMAP-826m.something — wait, that's outside this review's scope).
title: Single-user limitation disclosure in memory.rs:43-83 is exactly the right amount of disclosure for a reference impl
